findings.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:155 — The test asserts before joining the reader thread, so a late or unscheduled failing read is silently missed.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — The reader thread is neither coordinated to begin before deletion nor joined before assertion, so the regression test can pass without any concurrent read or after an unobserved failure.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — The reader thread is never synchronized or joined, so the assertion can run before it performs a read or before it records a concurrent failure.

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — The reader thread is neither coordinated to begin before deletion nor joined before assertion, so the regression test can pass without any concurrent read or after an unobserved failure.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real issue with the test design. Looking at the diff, the test creates a thread that reads groups while the main thread deletes them, but there's no synchronization to ensure the reader thread actually starts before deletions begin (no latch or barrier), and the thread is never joined before the assertion. This means the test could pass even if the reader thread never executes a single read, or if it throws exceptions after deletedAll is set to true but before the assertion. This is a legitimate test quality concern for a newly added test, not a hallucination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — The reader thread is never synchronized or joined, so the assertion can run before it performs a read or before it records a concurrent failure.

adjudication.rationale: The test creates a reader thread that loops while !deletedAll.get(), but after the deletion loop completes and deletedAll.set(true) is called, the assertion assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()) runs immediately without any Thread.join() or synchronization. This means: 1) The reader thread might not have started reading yet, 2) The reader thread might be mid-execution when the assertion runs, 3) Any exception caught after deletedAll is set but before the thread terminates won't be properly checked. This is a real concurrency bug in the test - the thread should be joined before asserting on caughtExceptions.
